messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 9:12 AM -0700
Subject: Capacity playback & pipeline handoff — weekly

Team —

Quick agenda for today's run-through: align this week's pipeline moves with fleet availability and lock any short-term commitments for DL-8472 (Orion.ai). Attached is the latest capacity playbook (Q2 v2) and the mutual action plan for DL-8472. Key asks:

- Infra: confirm whether we can guarantee 120k token-minutes / day for the Orion pilot windows (M-F 09:00-18:00 PT) without impacting current reserved customers.
- Finance: if we convert to a 6-month reserved commit for DL-8472, what changes to billing cadence / credit approvals are needed this week?
- Sales/Ops: confirm go-live date and procurement path from Orion; any blockers?

Notes: Fleet maintenance is scheduled the night of Apr 6 (ETA 02:00-04:00 PT); we need to decide if we shift pilot traffic or provide burst credits.

Action: can I get quick status updates by 2pm PT so I can respond to Orion's procurement team?

Thanks —
Jordan
Sr. Deal Lead, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_playbook_Q2_v2.pdf (pdf), DL-8472_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 11:03 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity playback & pipeline handoff — weekly

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. High level: 

- Current pool utilization: reserved pools at 72% average, burst capacity ~18% available across all GPU types.
- Short-term constraint: the Apr 6 maintenance will reduce total RTX-8000-equivalent capacity by ~9% for a 2-hour window. We can schedule Orion's heavier traffic to avoid that window or gate to a lower concurrency.
- Commitment ask: 120k token-minutes/day for a pilot is feasible if we reserve a temporary pool (3x G5-type nodes) and enable prefix caching for repeated prompt families. Ops will need a 48-hour lead to carve the pool.

Action items assigned: 
1) Karthik: validate the G5 node availability and confirm how many burst slots we can allocate without violating SLAs for existing reserved customers.
2) Ben: provide a runbook for on-call escalation if we exceed expected token-minutes during the pilot.
3) Neha: flag the billing implications if we move to a 6-month commit — can the contract team approve provisional credits this week?
4) Jordan/Laura: confirm Orion's official go-live window so I can schedule capacity carve.

I'll tentatively hold the pool pending Karthik's confirmation.

Irene Choi
Director, Deal Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 1:15 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity playback & pipeline handoff — weekly

Folks —

Quick infra readout: 
- G5 availability: we have 6 spare G5 nodes in OR-1 region this week; reserving 3 for Orion is safe if we stagger expected concurrency to their peak windows.
- Fallbacks: if demand spikes beyond the carved pool, we can route requests to a quantized Llama-2-70B variant that uses ~40% less memory and keep latency within SLO for customer-facing previews.
- Maintenance note: the Apr 6 maintenance is a firmware kernel update that affects NVLINK scheduling for ~2 hours. Recommend we shift full-load rehearsals to Apr 5 evening or reduce throughput during the maintenance window.

Runbook stub (attached):
- If live token-minutes exceed forecast by >20% for >10 minutes, throttle non-production traffic, notify CS and apply burst credits from the shared pool.
- If GPU memory pressure >85% for >5 minutes, fall back to quantized variant & scale horizontal instances.

I'll attach the infra runbook and the current node map. Ben

Ben Carter
Manager, Fleet Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fleet_runbook_apr_v1.md (md), node_map_OR-1.png (png)

Thanks team — appreciate the quick coordination. A couple items from Orion: 

- Timeline: pilot go-live target is Apr 12 for internal demos, public beta Apr 19. We need the reserved pilot capacity from Apr 12 through May 12.
- Required throughput: target steady-state 100k token-minutes/day, spikes up to 200k token-minutes during demo windows.
- Procurement: procurement@orion.ai can sign a 6-month reserve with milestone billing, but we need the DocuSign link and a note on provisional credits for the pilot period.

Can Redwood confirm the 3x G5 carve and provide the DocuSign this week? Also, if maintenance overlaps with Apr 12 rehearsals, we'll need a guaranteed fallback to the quantized variant.

Regards,
Sam Wong
Head of Product
Orion.ai

All —

Summary & decisions (finalized):
- Reserve: carve 3x G5 nodes in OR-1 for DL-8472 from 2027-04-12 through 2027-05-12. That maps to the pilot window Sam requested.
- Throughput guarantee: commit to steady-state 100k token-minutes/day; support demo spikes up to 200k with automatic fallback to quantized variant and burst credits applied.
- Maintenance: Apr 6 maintenance will not affect Apr 12 rehearsals; if the rehearsal schedule slips into the Apr 6 window, we'll provide a scheduled fallback lane and notify Orion.
- Billing: Neha to provision provisional credits for the pilot week and prepare contract language for 6-month reserved commit; Jordan to send DocuSign link by EOD Mon.
- Runbooks: Ben to publish the infra runbook and on-call escalation steps; Karthik to confirm node map and remaining burst capacity.

Action owners & due dates: 
- Jordan: DocuSign link + updated MAP -> due Mon 2027-04-05 11:00 PT
- Neha: provisional credits & contract draft -> due Tue 2027-04-06 10:00 PT
- Ben: publish runbook & node map -> due Mon 2027-04-05 16:00 PT
- Karthik: G5 confirmation & burst slots -> due Mon 2027-04-05 16:00 PT

I'll update the HubSpot deal (DL-8472) with these decisions and link the runbook. Thanks for the quick turn.

Irene Choi
